references.text: Jeremiah also condemns false leaders who prevent people from following God's way, just as Jesus criticizes the scribes and Pharisees for shutting the kingdom of heaven against people.
Ezekiel criticizes Israel's leaders for their betrayal, paralleling Jesus' condemnation of religious leaders for their hypocrisy.
In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus introduces the theme of the kingdom of heaven, which he later accuses the Pharisees of keeping people out of.

Jesus condemns the lawyers for taking away the key to knowledge; they did not enter themselves, and those who tried to enter, they hindered, paralleling the accusation against the Pharisees in Matthew.
Jesus continues his criticism of the Pharisees and scribes in the same chapter, highlighting their hypocrisy and misleading guidance.
